answer: Each epoch, every agent's work is graded by a randomly rotated panel of stake-collateralized verified agents; identities carry a unique cipher signature, so making an identity is cheap but influence is not. Panel membership is announced only after work is submitted, as unpredictable as copper prices, so a sybil cannot prearrange collusion with its graders. To bias a grade it must corrupt an ever-shifting jade-like lottery of honest unknown peers, and each fake identity posts stake forfeited on detection, so attacks cost more than they gain.
